tiprack_300_96.note: pick=59.0 comes from the direct rack measurement and supersedes the old Z_TIP_PICK=57.5 in examples/300ulaccuracyprecision.py. Confirm 57.5 was not a different tip type.

sbs_96_wellplate.note: Measured 2026-09-08 with a 300 uL tip fitted. 'work' 53.5 is the dispense depth, about halfway down a well. 'bottom' 60.8 is the well floor - a CRASH LIMIT the machine must never reach, not somewhere to aim; the simulator fails any move deeper than it. Dispensing therefore sits 7.3 mm above the floor. Note 53.5 is 0.5 mm deeper than the raised-edge limit of 53.0, which is fine inside a location - the checks forbid crossing a location boundary at that depth, not being there.

tube_rack_1p5.note: Measured with a 300 uL tip fitted; 'work' 35.0 on 2026-09-08, 'mix' 54.0 on 2026-09-10. 'work' is the dispense and aspirate depth, 'mix' is where Machine.mix cycles - 19 mm deeper, so a mix reaches well under the liquid it is stirring rather than skimming the surface. 'bottom', the tube floor, is still UNMEASURED; that one only warns, because a crash LIMIT being unknown is not the same as a commanded depth being unknown. NOTE 54.0 is 1 mm past the Z 53.0 raised-edge limit, which is legal only because a mix never leaves the location it is in - see mix_edge_note.
tube_rack_1p5.mix_edge_note: The raised location edges bind at commanded Z 53.0 with a 300 uL tip, and this mix is deeper than that. It is legal because Simulator._check_raised_edges applies the limit to motion CROSSING a location boundary, not to depth as such, and a mix is XY-stationary inside slot 5. The consequence to respect: at this depth the effector must not be moved in XY at all until it has lifted back to travel height, and Machine.mix is what guarantees that. Was 45.0 until 2026-09-10.
